summary: I walked RegExp.prototype[Symbol.replace] steps 1-17 and the GetSubstitution steps against the pinned spec text. The steps are implemented in order, with the observable Get/Set/Call/ToString/ToObject/ToLength calls in the spec's order and number. Abrupt completions propagate with `?`. The IsCallable-before-ToString ordering, the lastIndex resets, the empty-match AdvanceStringIndex path, the clamping of position, the captures loop, the functional and substitution branches, and the GetSubstitution $$, $`, $&, $', $n/$nn (including the two-digit fallback), and $<name> (including the not-found and undefined-groups fallbacks) are all as specified. No branch keys on test-specific inputs. Index arithmetic is guarded by the step 15.m check and the step 16 early return, so there are no reachable out-of-bounds panics. The single lint flag (unreachable!) is truly unreachable, because replace_value is rebound to a String exactly when functional_replace is false. The RegExp.prototype.flags getter is not implemented, so tests that need it fail with the engine's not-implemented error, which is honest partial work. Not verified: the behaviour of the external helpers regexp_exec, advance_string_index, length_of_array_like and key_from_index, which live outside this diff.
